programme: A visceral-smooth-muscle contractile module anchored on SRF target genes (ACTA2, TAGLN, CNN1, MYLK): MYOCD is the pro-differentiation SRF coactivator that switches these genes on, TCF21 is the antagonist that keeps mesenchymal/fibroblast-like cells undifferentiated by holding the same genes off, ELK4 is the alternative ETS/ternary-complex SRF cofactor that diverts SRF toward proliferative immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS) instead of the contractile set, FOXF1 is the upstream master regulator of splanchnic (gut/esophageal) mesenchyme that specifies this smooth-muscle lineage in the first place, GLI3/Hedgehog supplies the epithelial-to-mesenchyme patterning signal that induces that specification, and KLF13 co-activates the shared contractile target TAGLN.
role_in_a: In esophageal cancer this programme governs whether periepithelial/stromal mesenchyme stays a differentiated, contractile smooth-muscle/myofibroblast layer or converts to a proliferative, invasive phenotype. TCF21 repression of ACTA2/TAGLN/CNN1 and ELK4-driven immediate-early output push cells away from the MYOCD-differentiated state, consistent with GLI3 directly promoting ESCC metastasis and glycolysis (40222042, 34517880), KLF13 driving ESCC progression (40450000), TCF21 acting as an invasion suppressor when expressed (29909422), and FOXF1's established role in patterning the esophageal mesenchyme, disrupted forms of which cause esophageal structural anomalies (31993350, 26822871).
role_in_b: In Parkinson's disease the same contractile module operates in gut (gastric/esophageal) visceral smooth muscle, where dysmotility — delayed gastric emptying, dysphagia — is one of the most common non-motor features, plausibly reflecting loss of the MYOCD-driven contractile phenotype secondary to enteric/vagal dysfunction. This is directly evidenced by 42358150, in which a Parkinson's rat model shows an impaired gastric smooth-muscle contractile phenotype that is pharmacologically restored, in a context connected to MYOCD's target programme.
shared_axis: Esophageal cancer and Parkinson's disease both disturb the same MYOCD/SRF-anchored contractile-differentiation checkpoint in the gut wall's smooth muscle/mesenchyme — in cancer via TCF21/ELK4/GLI3-driven dedifferentiation of stroma toward an invasive phenotype, and in Parkinson's via enteric-driven loss of contractile identity in gastric/esophageal smooth muscle — so the same gene module is disrupted in each disease by a different upstream cause acting on shared tissue.
reasoning: The module is nameable independent of this pair (SRF/myocardin-vs-TCF21/ELK4 target-gene competition and FOXF1/GLI3 upstream patterning are established biology on their own), and the esophageal-cancer side is well anchored by direct, disease-specific PMIDs for GLI3, KLF13 and TCF21. The Parkinson's side is much thinner — only one paper (42358150) touches MYOCD-relevant smooth muscle in a PD model, and its relevance is flagged as uncertain from the abstract — so the cross-disease link rests more on the well-known clinical fact of PD gut dysmotility than on retrieved literature placing these specific factors in PD.
support: 40222042 (GLI3 phosphorylation by SRPK1 drives ESCC metastasis); 34517880 (GLI3-induced lncRNA drives ESCC glycolysis and progression); 29909422 (TCF21 expression inhibits invasion/metastasis in esophageal cancer); 40450000 (KLF13 promotes esophageal cancer progression and lipid metabolism reprogramming); 31993350 (FOXF1-linked esophageal atresia families show excess GI disease among relatives, tying FOXF1 to esophageal mesenchymal patterning); 26822871 (FOXF1 polymorphisms associate with esophageal acid reflux); 33851100 (ELK4 binding disruption reported in cancer, esophageal cancer among the cohorts, pan-cancer promoter-mutation study); 42358150 (Parkinson's rat model shows impaired gastric smooth-muscle contractile phenotype that treatment restores, though the paper's direct statement about MYOCD itself is not established from the text available).
how_to_falsify: Compare expression of the MYOCD/SRF contractile set (ACTA2, TAGLN, CNN1, MYLK) and TCF21/ELK4/MYOCD occupancy at their CArG/SRE promoter elements in ESCC tumor stroma versus matched normal esophageal smooth muscle (ChIP-qPCR or ChIP-seq plus RNA-seq); separately, assay the same contractile gene set and MYOCD expression in gastric/esophageal smooth muscle from PD patients or a vagal-denervation animal model versus controls. If neither tissue shows coordinated loss of the contractile set with altered TCF21/ELK4 versus MYOCD balance, the account is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|esophagus; the 207 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so many of those comparisons are non-independent subgroup splits of the same underlying cohorts and the concordance counts should not be read as 207 independent replications. MYOCD, FOXF1 and TCF21 are marked discordant rather than concordant — consistent with a module that is engaged in opposite directions in the two diseases (suppressed for invasion in cancer stroma, lost for contractility in PD gut smooth muscle) but this directional interpretation is inference, not something the discordant label states outright. TWIST1, NOTCH1 and SMAD3 — the more familiar EMT/Hedgehog co-regulators — were removed as tissue-generic, so GLI3 stands alone as the Hedgehog representative here and the account should not be read as invoking a fuller EMT/Notch programme. FGF2 and SOX5 are genuinely disease-associated (FGF2 in PD via 40248029/34459097; SOX5 in ESCC via 37531195) but their target sets (bone mineralization; chondrogenic/EMT) do not connect to this smooth-muscle module, so they were deliberately left out rather than overlooked.
